C-SEARCH-ERROR-VISIBILITY.Summary: Make folder search honest about failure and truncation: engine failures, invalid size limits and cancellation settle into distinct, localized UI states instead of rendering as "No results found", configured exclusions and size limits are actually applied by both search engines, cancellation stops a silent rg child promptly, and the dead legacy sidebar search panel is removed in the same zone.
C-SEARCH-ERROR-VISIBILITY.Problem: Confirmed against the current read-only state of the canary-beta-wave tree; source findings are audits integration-reliability F-012/F-014, config-hygiene F-003/F-004 and dead-code F-001 (2026-11-20). In src-tauri/src/m013b/search.rs the rg transport run_ripgrep_with_program pipes stderr to Stdio::null(), breaks the read loop silently on a stream error, ignores child.wait(), and always returns Ok(total) — rg exit code 2 (bad pattern, unreadable tree) is indistinguishable from exit 1 (no matches), so the session coordinator emits "complete" and the renderer shows an empty result set. Cancellation flips the registry flag, but the flag is checked only inside the blocking reader.lines() loop, so a quiet rg child keeps running and the cancelled terminal waits for its next output line. SearchOptions carries exclusions, but neither engine applies them: the embedded walker never tests entry paths against the masks and BUILD_RIPGREP_COMMAND adds no glob-exclusion arguments. The renderer sends preferencesStore.searchMaxFileSize verbatim as the documented size string ("123", "1K", "2M", "3G"; _shims/preferences/schema.json) while the Rust field is Option u64, so any non-empty limit fails spawn deserialization, the invoke rejects, and src/renderer/src/store/search.js catches the error by clearing results and logging — this.error is never set. The live surface src/renderer/src/components/projectSearch/index.vue destructures the store's error state but its template renders only "Searching…", "No results found." and the result summary, so every failure mode — dead rg binary, permission-denied sweep, invalid limit, engine exit 2 — is displayed as an ordinary empty search; the hardcoded English "Showing first 100 results only" throttle string is the only error-ish state today. Separately, dead-code F-001: src/renderer/src/components/sideBar/search.vue and searchToolbar.vue mount only in tests (the sidebar shell is Files-only since C-40 T-003; the live overlay is ProjectSearch mounted from pages/app.vue), and the locale keys sideBar.search.startTyping and sideBar.search.openFolder are read by nothing else.
C-SEARCH-ERROR-VISIBILITY.Relationship: Direct successor of C-SEARCH-SESSION-COMPLETION (merged as #289, status applied): that change gave SearchSessionCoordinator ownership of the session-wide seq and the single terminal; this change keeps that ownership untouched and fills the terminal with honest content — an engine error terminal with a stable message, a cancelled terminal that arrives promptly, and an optional partial marker so already-streamed hits are never presented as the complete answer. It reuses the session coordinator's voice and test seams (run_session_with_program injection, ChannelSink/HookSink full-trace collectors). Related debt, recorded but not absorbed: the two engines differ (rg shell-out vs embedded walker) and stay unmerged — see NonGoals. Related and unabsorbed: C-SEARCH-INPUT-COMPOSITION-CONTRACT lives in the separate search-input-composition worktree with its own exclusion/size implementation; the plan must rebase this change onto the actual delivery baseline it selects, as in the predecessor spec. The dead-panel removal is dead-code F-001 riding the same zone; it is conditional on the plan re-verifying the death evidence on the delivery baseline. Delivered through the repository technical-debt lane; lane departure into main and train accounting are separate owner-controlled steps.

Goals.Goal: An engine failure (spawn failure, rg exit code 2, unreadable output stream, invalid pattern) ends the session through the existing coordinator with exactly one error terminal carrying a stable, non-empty message; codes 0 and 1 remain normal completion (1 = no matches). The renderer shows a distinct, localized failure state for that searchId and never shows the plain "No results found." message for a failed search; already-streamed hits are marked as partial, not silently kept or silently dropped.

Cancellation settles promptly: a requested cancel terminates the rg child even while it produces no output, reaps it, and delivers the single cancelled terminal without waiting for the next stdout line. The embedded walker keeps its existing between-files cancel checks. Cancel stays idempotent, harmless for unknown ids, and the coordinator remains the only terminal emitter.

Configured search limits apply honestly: exclusion masks are honored identically by both engines (excluded files skipped, sibling matches retained), and maxFileSize reaches Rust as the documented size format parsed at the renderer IPC boundary (plain bytes plus K/M/G suffixes), with an invalid limit producing a clear localized message instead of an aborted-then-empty search. When a size limit or exclusion actually suppresses what would otherwise be searched, or an engine error leaves hits already streamed, the result set is flagged as partial through an additive optional wire field and the UI says so honestly.

The dead legacy sidebar search panel is removed in the same zone once the plan re-confirms F-001 on the delivery baseline: delete src/renderer/src/components/sideBar/search.vue and searchToolbar.vue with their four dedicated test files and the two orphaned locale keys in all ten locales. The shared search store, searchResultItem.vue and the live ProjectSearch overlay stay.

Keep the existing renderer thenable/cancel contract, per-search searchId filtering, stale-generation protection and unsubscribe behavior; keep the in-document find bar (components/search/index.vue) and its suites untouched.

Constraints.Constraint: Keep the existing command names (mt_search_spawn, mt_search_cancel), the mt::search-event channel, searchId, kind values (match/complete/cancelled/error), hits and error payload fields, batch size, per-line cap, root validation via M-010, engine selection (App Store in-process, missing-rg fallback with BLOCK_RIPGREP_FALLBACK) and ordinary root traversal order. Do not add a new terminal kind or a second event channel.

The rg spawn contract is unchanged except for the two fixes that require it, justified here: (a) stderr is captured (bounded) and the child exit status is checked after wait, because error visibility is impossible while stderr is discarded and the status ignored; (b) a bounded cancellation watcher thread kills the child on the cancel flag, because the cancel check cannot run while the main thread blocks in reader.lines() on a silent child. Both changes stay inside run_ripgrep_with_program and preserve the --json argument set and all existing option flags; the fix requires no new rg flag beyond what the options already map to.

Partial honesty uses one additive optional field on the existing SearchEvent envelope (absent-field serialization preserved via skip_serializing_if); the window shim translation branch for mt::search-event and the legacy searcher's error payload propagate it without changing the class API or any other channel.

Exclusion masks are applied symmetrically: the walker filters entries against the compiled masks; the rg path passes them as exclusion glob arguments. Mask semantics (case sensitivity, matching against the path relative to its root) are defined once and shared, and a mask that fails to compile is reported as a clear error or explicitly ignored per the plan's documented choice — never silently dropped while results look complete.

maxFileSize parsing happens in the renderer before invoke, implementing the documented format from the preferences schema; the Rust Option u64 field and the --max-filesize/walker max_filesize application stay as they are. An invalid limit yields a localized message and no spawn.

Renderer failure states are localized: new keys under the existing sideBar.search namespace in all ten locale files (en, de, es, fr, ja, ko, pt, ru, zh-CN, zh-TW), following the C-62 all-locales pattern and gated by the locale-keys test. Error and partial copy describes the failure class and, where present, that shown results are incomplete; query text, match contents and user paths stay out of diagnostic fields and messages.

Respect existing cancellation timing budgets, batch bounds, registry lifecycle (insert on spawn, remove after the worker finishes) and the 120 ms listen warm-up. The cancel watcher must not remove registry entries early, must not emit terminals, and must exit after kill and wait.

Baseline divergence: the search-input-composition worktree (C-SEARCH-INPUT-COMPOSITION-CONTRACT, dated 2026-11-16) carries exclusion-glob implementation in its src-tauri/src/m013b/search.rs and size/exclusions ingress tests absent from the current tree. NonGoals.NonGoal: No unification of the two search engines (rg shell-out vs embedded walker). The known divergence is recorded as related debt in the relationship section and stays open; this change only makes their observable limit/error behavior symmetric. No rg sidecar bundling (B4), no search ranking, no new search features, no regex syntax changes, no context-line delivery.

No rework of the unreachable "first 100 results" throttle (the Rust path emits no searchedPaths events, so the legacy didSearchPaths cap cannot fire; the typed facade synthesizes counts instead) — recorded as an observation for the plan, not changed here beyond leaving it harmless.

No change to preferences storage or schema shape, document saves, workspace root ownership, C-50 signing boundary, dependency acquisition, release version, tags or publication; no absorption of C-SEARCH-INPUT-COMPOSITION-CONTRACT and no redesign of the typed ipcSearch facade beyond its read-only status.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Failing-first backend tests prove error is not empty: an injected rg program that exits 2 (or a real rg with an invalid regex under the existing availability guard) yields exactly one error terminal with a non-empty stable message, zero post-terminal events, remaining roots not started, and the terminal carries the partial marker when hits were already streamed; codes 0 and 1 keep completing normally for both engines.

A cancellation test with a deterministic silent rg child (injection seam, no PATH mutation) proves the child is killed and reaped and the single cancelled terminal arrives without waiting for child output; pre-cancel, mid-stream, between-roots, repeated and post-completion cancellation keep exactly one terminal (existing suites stay green).

Exclusion tests pin both engines: a masked file is absent while an unmasked sibling with the same needle is present, in the walker and in rg (availability-guarded), with identical mask semantics; a documented invalid mask is reported or explicitly ignored per the plan's recorded choice.

Size-limit tests pin the renderer boundary: "1048576", "1K", "2M", "3G" parse and pass; an invalid limit produces a localized error state and no spawn; a valid limit that suppresses candidates marks the result set partial and the UI states it.

Renderer tests pin error visibility: an engine rejection sets the store's error state for the surviving generation and ProjectSearch renders the localized failure line instead of "No results found."; a cancelled search resolves quietly without a failure message; stale generations still cannot write; the partial notice renders from the additive envelope field through the shim and legacy searcher without API change.

Dead-panel removal tests: the two legacy components and their four test files are gone, the two locale keys are absent from all ten locales, and the live surfaces (ProjectSearch overlay, searchResultItem, sidebar tree, in-document find bar suites, commands heading-search and e2e search-bar) stay green.

Graph ownership, module maps and verification entries (M-004, M-011, M-013, V-M-004, V-M-011) describe the final implementation; all pre-existing search suites — the C-SEARCH-SESSION-COMPLETION session-trace family, options/gitignore/bounds families and the V-M-011 chrome command — pass without weakened assertions or budgets.

Existing session-trace, cancellation and renderer regression receipts are preserved as pre-change evidence, not relabeled.

App Store and missing-rg fallback paths exercised at least through the embedded-walker unit suites; native rg behavior guarded by the existing availability checks. Unavailable platform or owner acceptance evidence remains explicitly open and is not substituted by a shim.

Assumptions.Assumption: The rg exit-status contract (0 match, 1 no match, 2 error) established by the audit's local rg 13.0.0 reproduction and the BurntSushi changelog is treated as the rg transport contract; the plan verifies it once on the delivery baseline before pinning tests.

The dead-panel death evidence (no production importer, two orphaned keys) is verified in the current tree on 2026-11-21 and must be re-verified by the plan on the delivery baseline; approval of this specification does not approve an unwritten plan, apply/archive, lane departure or release.

Error and partial copy wording per locale is plan and implementation detail; the specification pins key presence, all-ten-locale coverage and the distinct-from-empty rendering contract, not the translations.
